query: Hindenburg short seller report on Equinix

output.content:
**Hindenburg’s short report on Equinix (NASDAQ: EQIX)** was published on **March 20, 2024**, under the title *“Equinix Exposed: Major Accounting Manipulation, Core Business Decay And Selling An AI Pipe Dream As Insiders Cashed Out Hundreds of Millions.”* [[1]]

**The core allegation was that Equinix materially overstated adjusted funds from operations (AFFO), a key non-GAAP/REIT cash-flow metric, by at least 22% in 2023.** [[1]] Hindenburg alleged that the principal mechanism was misclassifying recurring maintenance capital expenditure as non-recurring/growth capital expenditure, which reduces the AFFO deduction for maintenance spending and raises reported AFFO. [[1]] 

Hindenburg further alleged that Equinix capitalized operating expenses that should have been expensed, inflating both reported operating profitability and AFFO. [[1]] It argued that the alleged accounting choices were economically significant because executive compensation incorporated AFFO targets, and claimed executives had received compensation linked to those metrics while insiders sold substantial amounts of stock. [[1]] [[2]] 

The report also challenged the strategic narrative around AI, contending that power constraints and competition/commoditization in Equinix’s traditional colocation and interconnection business limited its ability to benefit from AI-related data-center demand. [[3]] [[1]] Hindenburg said its work included reviews of financial and litigation records plus interviews with **37 former employees, industry experts and competitors**. [[1]]

**Market and company response:** EQIX closed down **2.3% to $824.88** on the publication day after trading as low as $796.90, according to contemporaneous reporting. [[3]] Equinix initially said it was reviewing the assertions, then announced on **March 25, 2024** that its Audit Committee had begun an independent investigation. [[3]] [[4]] 

Equinix subsequently disclosed that it received a subpoena from the **U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of California** shortly after the report and, on **April 30, 2024**, a subpoena from the **SEC**. [[5]] [[6]] Its March 2025 Form 10-Q stated that it was cooperating fully with both agencies. [[6]]

**Outcome of the internal review:** In its first-quarter 2024 disclosure, Equinix said that its Audit Committee, assisted by independent third-party professional advisers, had substantially completed the investigation and concluded that Equinix’s financial reporting was accurate and that its accounting practices appropriately represented operating performance. [[5]] Equinix’s 2025 proxy reiterated that conclusion and noted that the Audit Committee held 36 meetings during 2024, with the unusually high number related to the short-report investigation. [[7]]

**Bottom line:** Hindenburg presented a bear case centered on the reliability of AFFO, capital-expenditure classification, expense capitalization, executive incentives, and the durability of the AI-growth thesis. [[1]] Equinix’s board-led independent investigation rejected the accounting allegations in substance, but the company’s later filings still disclosed ongoing cooperation with the DOJ and SEC subpoenas rather than a publicly stated final governmental resolution. [[5]] [[8]]
